chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Flipping the record: In The Mood becomes the A side
summary: An Oklahoma City DJ suggests flipping the record; Pierce agrees and In The Mood takes off.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: We had a background and Rene laughed, he said you've just got to have somebody singing or something so we put a little humming in there. I'll tell you about how it went. We got a good review in Billboard also and so they made Christopher number one--I mean A. So they were playing it and a DJ was in Oklahoma City, he used to be in Tulsa, and he knew me personally and he played it, he played around with Christopher for a week or two, and then he played In The Mood, but he never would play it on the air, like the company told him.
Yeah, the company always designated A and B.

So he called me up and finally got a hold of me and said, Ernie, I have your new record, I think both of them are real nice, but I would like to flip and make In The Mood the A side. He said I don't know why but I just think it has a jump on Christopher. He said Christopher is a good number but it never was as big as In The Mood was, and I believe that new version that you have has to make it, with the name, I think it will make it.

I said let me call Rod Pierce and I called Rod Pierce up and Rod said Ernie, anything you think if it will help, go ahead. By then I think it had been out about three months and hadn't done anything. They guy over at WKY in Oklahoma City flipped that side and the first round he made the green light came on,and then I called Rod and told him and Rod then called everywhere and told them to flip it, play In The Mood. And from then on there was no turning back.
